notes:
Account snapshot: Peregrine builds low-latency conversational assistants for institutional traders and customer support bots that access sensitive market and transaction data. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and strict residency. Primary ask: committed GPU capacity with guaranteed throughput and P99 latency SLOs plus clear unit economics per token. They care about predictable monthly cost and the option to burst to hosted for peak events.

Cost modeling discussion highlights: Alex and Priya walked through a 3-slab commit proposal in the shared spreadsheet: 10, 30, 60 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs. Baseline assumptions: 60% average utilization for chat workload (conservative), 80% for nightly batch embedding jobs, mixed model mix: 50% small chat model (7B/13B quantized), 30% 70B for complex summarization, 20% embedding model (up to 4096-d). Token mix assumptions: avg request length 120 tokens, avg response 220 tokens -> 340 tokens per request. Expected steady-state qps: 450 requests/minute during trading hours -> nominal tokens/sec estimate ~2550 tokens/sec.

Unit economics shown in spreadsheet: reserved amortized cost per GPU (3-yr commit) -> $Xk/month (placeholder until finance pricing). Using Redwood suggestion for caching and batching optimizations, model-level token cost reduced by 18-25% vs naive serving. Break-even sensitivity: if utilization <40% cost per token jumps by ~60%, if utilization >75% cost/token falls by ~35%. We modeled mixed routing where high-priority traffic pinned to dedicated GPUs and lower-tier routed to hosted.

SLA / negotiation notes: client is pushing for 99.95% availability SLA and P95 chat latency <120ms, P99 <350ms for 4k context models. They want automatic fallback to hosted API when Dedicated capacity exhausted with transparent accounting for egress and token billing. Legal flagged data residency: logs must stay in US region and KMS keys customer-managed.

POC plan: 2-week Dedicated POC on 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent) with synthetic and replayed production traces. Deliverables: latency p50/p95/p99 telemetry, throughput curves at different batch sizes, cost per token estimate for steady-state and peak, guidance doc with recommended commit level and expected ARR impact.

Sales cues / quotes: "We need to avoid surprise bills during market open spikes — predictable monthly is a must." — Head of Platform.

CRM shorthand: evaluating three-commit scenarios, strong preference for VPC/private control plane, legal/residency gating, finance waiting for final price book.
